blocks.x: Portfolio optimization rebuilt quantum-inspired, treaty-mix scenario runs from nine hours to 22 minutes and the hedging review moves into the quarter

A global reinsurer: Insurers feel process gaps in loss adjustment expense and customer churn, both of them slow, both of them measurable. The Achala program started with the claims journey —. The baseline signed in week two made the cost visible in units the finance team already owns, and the engagement ran under the standard Achala charter — a named metric, a named control owner and gates that evidence every move.
The baseline was the overnight run itself: nine hours per scenario, so capital committees saw two scenarios per month and hedging decisions were made on instinct between runs.
The solver's heuristics had been tuned for a smaller book; adding cedents made runs slower and the team quietly reduced scenario breadth to keep the calendar.

We rebuilt the optimization as a quantum-inspired decomposition: the treaty mix decomposed into tractable sub-problems solved in parallel, constraint handling moved into the formulation so feasibility was guaranteed rather than repaired, and the scenario library ran as a service with results reproducible seed-by-seed. The capital committee now reviews live scenarios, not last month's.
